the EPIRB — a cell that calls for help when everything else fails
the IFR — a cell whose value is the rules you follow when you cannot see
the VHF radio — a cell that lets you talk to other boats
the aileron — a cell that turns the wing into a rudder
the altimeter — a cell whose value is the height of the air
the anchor — a cell that holds the boat to the bottom
the autopilot — a cell that is also a captain
the beacon — a cell whose only job is to be the address
the bilge pump — a cell that keeps the boat from sinking
the carburetor — a cell that turns fuel into flight
the cargo pod — a cell that holds the payload away from the wing
the ceiling — a cell whose value is the height you cannot go above
the chartplotter — a cell that draws the map as you sail
the climb rate — a cell that measures how fast you are gaining height
the cockpit — a cell that is the bridge between the captain and the sky
the compass — a cell whose value is the direction of the magnetic north
the control tower — a cell that is the bridge between the captain and the dispatcher
the crosswind — a cell that pushes the aircraft sideways
the dead reckoning — a cell whose value is where I would be if I were still
the descent — a cell whose value is the rate at which you are losing height
the diesel engine — a cell that turns fuel into motion
the elevator — a cell that makes the nose go up or down
the engine — a cell that turns fuel into flight
the fathometer — a cell that measures the depth of the water below
the flaps — a cell that changes the shape of the wing
the flight level — a cell whose value is a pressure altitude
the fuel — a cell whose value is the energy you have left
the galley — a cell that cooks while the boat moves
the glide ratio — a cell that measures how far you can go without power
the hangar — a cell that holds the aircraft when it is not flying
the heading indicator — a cell that points to the direction of the flight
the headsail — a cell that catches the wind ahead of the mast
the horizontal stabilizer — a cell that keeps the nose from going up or down
the keel — a cell that keeps the boat from sliding sideways
the mast — a cell that holds the sail up to the wind
the navigation lights — a cell that tells other boats where you are
the outhaul — a cell that pulls the foot of the sail out to the end of the boom
the propeller — a cell that pushes the boat through the water
the rode — a cell that connects the anchor to the boat
the stern — a cell that is the back of the boat
the tiller — a cell that turns the rudder with your hand
the watermaker — a cell that turns seawater into drinking water
the winch — a cell that gives you mechanical advantage
the x-track — a cell that is the line you want to follow
